message.content: The evidence is decisive: two confirmed in-scope claims (c1, c2) show the kernel violates the contract's fixed 1e-6 absolute tolerance on many ordinary in-domain FP16 inputs in both the middle interval and the upper branch, with worst errors up to 5e-6 (5x the tolerance). The problem.txt explicitly makes this a single global verdict over every finite FP16 value, so no distribution caveat can rescue it. Skeptic has signed off with no new claims and all claims have evidence. Recording a reject verdict.

function.arguments: {"confidence": 0.97, "decisive_claims": ["c1", "c2"], "reason": "The contract (problem.txt) requires abs(actual[i] - atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 value, as a single global verdict. These are ordinary, in-domain FP16 values, not edge cases; the failures are systematic (hundreds to thousands of lattice points), not single-point ties or negligible near-zero absolute differences — errors reach 3-5x the tolerance. c3 (extrema ±65504) was rebutted (error only ~5e-8), showing the defect is in the FP32 rational evaluation in the middle and upper intervals, not at the extremes. All open claims have evidence, and the Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims. The declared contract permits approximations but only if they meet the 1e-6 absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain; the confirmed evidence shows they do not.
